statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 4, low, because CME equity index futures have been halted since Friday at 21:00Z and the six slots up to the scheduled 22:00Z reopen contain no tradable Nasdaq-100 interval at all; the eighteen slots from the reopen onward carry conditional Tail readings between 10 and 15, all far below the block threshold. Stress is 39, moderate: Friday's long-end yield stress, Brent near 94 dollars and a reported Monday US briefing on isolating Iran's economy are unpriced until the venue reopens. Confidence is 85, high, on verified index, volatility, yield, oil and calendar levels, limited only by the absence of a live price path.
recommendation: The last observed session remains consistent with functioning mean reversion rather than a one-way path: cash NDX opened at 29,359.60, traded down to 29,142.44, recovered to 29,405.12 and closed at 29,308.86, up 0.33% on the day and below its own open, while the VIX settled near 15 after a 14.77-15.95 range. Both session extremes were retraced, so no persistent directional efficiency is on record. Tail-relevant structure cannot be observed again until the 22:00Z reopen, and the narrow evidence-based danger window covers 22:00Z to 02:00Z, when the weekend information set is repriced into thin liquidity.
headline: Closed-venue assessment with eighteen reopen hours inside the horizon: Tail holds the floor of 4 through six shut hours, then carries conditional readings between 10 and 15 from the 22:00Z Sunday reopen through a US cash open and first cash hour that now sit inside the window, while a faded Treasury buyback rally, Brent at its highest of the month and a reported Monday US briefing on isolating Iran's economy stay unpriced.
body: CME Globex equity index futures stopped trading for the week on Friday at 21:00Z and are scheduled to reopen on Sunday at 22:00Z. The twenty-four slots published here run from 2026-08-23T16:00:00Z to 2026-08-24T15:00:00Z, so the reopen slot and the seventeen hours after it sit inside the horizon while the first six do not, and the US cash open at 13:30Z plus the first two cash hours now fall inside the window. Cash NDX settled at 29,308.86 on Friday, up 0.33% from a 29,213.17 prior close, having opened at 29,359.60 and traded a 29,142.44 to 29,405.12 range; both extremes were retraced and the index finished below its own open, which is mean-reverting rather than one-way behaviour. The broader tape agreed: S&P 500 +0.43% at 7,674.37, Nasdaq Composite +0.43% at 26,180.46, Dow +0.98%, yet the Nasdaq lost 2.0% on the week and the S&P 500 1.4%. Volatility compressed into the close, with the VIX near 15 after a 14.77-15.95 range and a 15.84 prior close. The dominant macro channel is the long end of the Treasury curve: the 30-year finished the week near 5.27% and the 10-year near 4.73% after an expanded Treasury buyback programme produced only temporary relief, while the H.15 release shows the 2-year at 4.19% and the 10-year at 4.69% for 20 August. Energy is the second channel, with WTI at 87.06 dollars and Brent at 94.39 dollars on Friday, Brent's fifth consecutive advance and its highest level this month, ahead of a reported Monday US press conference detailing plans to isolate Iran's economy. Delayed weekend cross-asset context shows last-session gains in index futures with the VIX future lower, gold higher and Treasury futures lower, alongside mixed megacaps and slightly negative semiconductors; that context is supporting evidence only and cannot establish live structure. Because no Nasdaq-100 price can print before 22:00Z, current Tail stays at its structural floor of 4 and the mapped policy state is EA_ON. Conditional Tail peaks at 13 in the first full hour after the reopen, decays to 10 through the Asian session, then rebuilds to 14 at the US cash open and 15 in the final slot as a full US session's structural possibilities accumulate. The week's largest catalysts, the July PCE report and Nvidia's results on Wednesday and the Warsh Jackson Hole keynote on Friday, all sit beyond this horizon and are carried in the event calendar.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is partial: 19 hourly assessments are available, while the 21:00Z clock-hour on 22 August and the 07:00Z, 10:00Z, 11:00Z and 12:00Z clock-hours on 23 August have no published assessment and are marked unavailable. Across every available hour Tail held 4 and the mapped policy state stayed EA_ON, so no hour approached the block threshold and the dominant mode remained normal throughout. Stress decayed steadily across the shut weekend, from 41 at the start of the window to a low of 34 in the early European hours, then turned higher into the afternoon and reached 38 in the most recent published hour as the reopen drew closer. Confidence eased from 87 to 85 as the last observed session receded further into the past.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail at 4 because CME equity index futures are confirmed halted and no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop inside this slot. The next five slots describe the same closed market, so Tail holds 4 and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout them, while Stress rises from 39 to 46 as the reopen approaches with the weekend information set unpriced. The final eighteen slots are tradable: the 22:00Z scheduled reopen carries a conditional Tail of 12 and the first full hour after it 13, the horizon's early peak, on the untested assumption that a weekend gap could extend before retracing. Conditional Tail then decays to 10 through the Asian hours, where two-way trade is historically most reliable, before rebuilding through the European session to 14 at the 13:30Z US cash open and 15 in the closing slot. Stress follows a similar shape, peaking at 49 just after the reopen, easing to 43 overnight and reaching 51 in the US cash hours. Every forecast Tail stays inside the low band, so no slot maps to a block state; the danger window is kept narrow at 22:00Z to 02:00Z, covering the reopen repricing rather than the whole session.
